q: Which statement about kidney development is FALSE?
o: Nephrons come from mesenchyme, ducts from bud
All three kidneys come from intermediate mesoderm
Nephrogenesis goes on for two years after birth
The oldest nephrons lie deep, near the medulla
e: Kidneys appear in order: pronephros, mesonephros, metanephros; the first two regress; all come from intermediate mesoderm. The metanephros forms in the sacral region when the ureteric bud sprouts from the distal nephric duct and meets metanephric mesenchyme (book: about 4 weeks). Glomerulus, proximal tubule, loop of Henle and distal tubule come from metanephric mesenchyme; collecting ducts, calyces, pelvis and ureter from the bud. Older, more mature nephrons are inner (juxtamedullary). Nephrogenesis is completed before birth; maturation continues postnatally.

q: Which statement contrasting congenital with acquired obstruction is FALSE?
o: Only congenital obstruction alters glomeruli
Acquired obstruction shows lymphocyte infiltrate
The developing kidney may never fully recover
Congenital obstruction shows heavy inflammation
e: Congenital obstruction lacks a significant inflammatory infiltrate unless infected; postnatal acquired obstruction commonly shows interstitial lymphocytes. Only congenital obstruction alters glomerular development; acquired obstruction can only damage an established pattern. Key features of congenital obstruction: altered growth regulation, differentiation and functional integration (with interstitial fibrosis, tubular hypotrophy, more epithelial–mesenchymal transformation). Effects in the developing kidney may be irreversible.

q: Which statement about corticosteroids in genital dermatology is FALSE?
o: Oral steroid effects last 8 to 48 hours
Split daily doses limit adrenal suppression
Peak blood levels occur 30–90 min after a dose
Topical steroids can be absorbed systemically
e: For short courses (≤3 weeks, e.g., allergic contact dermatitis) give a single morning dose to minimise hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal suppression. Oral steroids are absorbed in the jejunum, peak at 30–90 min, have plasma half-lives of 1–5 h but act for 8–48 h. Topical steroids can be absorbed with systemic effects. Periodic acid–Schiff (PAS) staining of skin scrapings identifies fungi such as Candida and dermatophytes.

q: Which statement about diagnosing ureteropelvic junction (UPJ) obstruction is FALSE?
o: Most new cases follow antenatal scans
Diuretic renography quantifies drainage
MCDK cysts connect with one another
Whitaker perfusion runs at 10 mL per min
e: Maternal ultrasonography detects most asymptomatic newborn hydronephrosis. Diuretic renography assesses drainage and function; US, CT and retrograde pyelography are only anatomical. Whitaker test (via nephrostomy, 10 mL/min): <15 cmH2O non-obstructed, >22 cmH2O obstructed, between = indeterminate; ideal when a nephrostomy is already in place. On US, hydronephrotic 'cysts' connect; MCDK cysts are separate.

q: Which statement about sacral neuromodulation (SNM) is FALSE?
o: Mild MS with no MRI needs may suit it
It is approved for neurogenic bladder
Atonic diabetic bladders respond poorly
Use in children is limited by growth data
e: SNM is an established third-line option for idiopathic bladder dysfunction: FDA-approved for idiopathic OAB and nonobstructive retention (also faecal incontinence), not for bladder pain/interstitial cystitis or neurogenic bladder (IC benefit reported; may expand). The end organ must work: an areflexic diabetic bladder with retention responds poorly. Best MS candidate: mild symptoms, good mobility, no future MRI need. Children: off-label; limited by lack of data on spinal growth and lead position; noninvasive therapies need repeated sessions.

q: Which statement about arterial anatomy at radical prostatectomy is FALSE?
o: Capsular vessels mark the cavernous nerves
Aberrant pudendals may arise from obturator
Accessory pudendal arteries are best divided
The inferior vesical artery feeds the prostate
e: The prostate is supplied by the inferior vesical artery. Capsular arteries and veins run posterolaterally in the lateral pelvic fascia, wrapped in nerves: the macroscopic landmark for the cavernous nerves. The corpora are mainly supplied by the internal pudendal artery, but aberrant/accessory pudendals can arise from obturator, inferior vesical or superior vesical arteries; they run on the anterolateral prostate and should be preserved, especially in older men with borderline penile flow.

q: Which statement about renal developmental genes is TRUE?
o: GDNF arrests ureteric bud growth in vitro
WT1 mutant mice form normal ureteric buds
p53 knockout mice lack both their kidneys
Pax-2 knockouts form no nephric ducts
e: Pax-2 knockout: no nephric ducts, müllerian ducts, ureteric buds or metanephric mesenchyme; death within a day from renal failure. WT1 mutants form no ureteric buds. GDNF (RET ligand, secreted by metanephric mesenchyme) promotes bud growth; GDNF knockouts have impaired bud formation. p53 knockouts have no major renal anomaly. The renin-angiotensin system is needed for normal renal growth. Human WT1 defects cause hypospadias, cryptorchidism and disorders of sex development.

q: Which statement about laparoscopic pyeloplasty in children is FALSE?
o: Robotic assistance eases the anastomosis
Transperitoneal visibility is usually poor
Posterior access is hard in horseshoe kidney
Benefit over open in infants is unproven
e: The peritoneum reflects light, so transperitoneal visibility is better than retroperitoneal. In newborns open access needs only a small incision; laparoscopy is feasible but advantages in infants are unproven. Posterior access to the UPJ is very difficult in horseshoe kidneys. Dismembered pyeloplasty is favoured: broadly applicable, excises the abnormal segment, allows reduction. Laparoscopic repair matches open results with good cosmesis; robotics eases suturing.

q: Which statement about genital dermatitis is FALSE?
o: Nickel is the commonest patch-test allergen
Patch tests confirm allergic contact type
Allergic type is the commonest contact form
Emollients are the mainstay for atopic eczema
e: Irritant contact dermatitis (direct cytotoxic effect of soaps, metal salts, acids/alkalis, solvents) causes about 80% of contact dermatitis. Patch testing confirms allergic contact dermatitis and the allergen; nickel sulfate (jewellery, belt buckles) was the commonest in the NACDG 2003 report. Atopic dermatitis: intense pruritus, asthma/rhinitis tendency; remove triggers, gentle non-alkali soaps and frequent emollients.

q: Which statement about obstruction-related renal dysplasia is TRUE?
o: Heterotopic bone is a hallmark feature of it
Partial late obstruction is its main cause
Small obstructed kidneys reflect true atrophy
Fibromuscular collars are typical
e: Fibromuscular collars (primitive ducts from abnormal peritubular mesenchyme) are a hallmark; heterotopic cartilage (not bone) may occur; glomerular cysts are not typical. Complete obstruction early in gestation is a critical determinant. Small congenitally obstructed kidneys are hypoplastic (growth failure), not atrophic; growth impairment means fewer nephrons and delayed maturation. Excess renin can occur in obstruction without dysplasia.

q: Which statement about endopyelotomy is FALSE?
o: Bleeding may need early angiography after it
Crossing vessels hardly affect success
Strictures over 2 cm usually do poorly
Most failures appear in the first year
e: A crossing vessel has the most detrimental effect on success, as does high-grade hydronephrosis; excluding these improves results (CT angiography assesses vessels). For a young patient with a crossing vessel, laparoscopic pyeloplasty is the straightforward choice. Success in selected patients is 60–80%; most failures occur within a year. Long (>2 cm) strictures do poorly; access across the UPJ must be secured first. Balloon dilation: only 42% long-term success (McClinton). Low threshold for angioembolisation if bleeding.

q: Which statement about nerve anatomy at radical prostatectomy is FALSE?
o: Slow-twitch fibres give passive continence
Bundles lie between prostatic and levator fascia
The pudendal nerve supplies the sphincter
The pelvic plexus arises from T11 to L2
e: The pelvic plexus carries parasympathetic preganglionic fibres from S2–S4. The neurovascular bundles run in the lateral pelvic fascia between the prostatic and levator fasciae. The pudendal nerve is the main supply of the striated sphincter and levator ani; the striated sphincter's fatigue-resistant slow-twitch fibres provide passive urinary control.

q: Which statement is FALSE?
o: Neuromodulation alters neurotransmission
Rhizotomy can make a bladder areflexic
Neurostimulation gives a delayed response
The guarding reflex promotes urine storage
e: Neurostimulation aims at an immediate response in neurogenic dysfunction; neuromodulation alters neurotransmission (neurogenic and non-neurogenic) with a delayed effect. Guarding reflex and bladder afferent loop reflex (sacral interneurons to pudendal efferents) promote storage under sympathetic tone and are switched off (suprapontine input) during voiding. Bilateral anterior and posterior sacral rhizotomy or conusectomy converts hyperreflexia to areflexia but harms rectum, sphincters, sexual function and legs; selective motor section was meant to spare these.

q: Which statement about erythema multiforme (EM) is FALSE?
o: HSV precedes target lesions by about 2 weeks
EM minor resolves in weeks without treatment
Late acyclovir speeds healing of EM
NSAIDs are among common triggers of SJS
e: EM minor: abrupt symmetrical fixed red papules evolving to target lesions; most follow HSV-1/2 by 10–14 days. Suppressive acyclovir may prevent episodes, but giving it after targets appear does not help; it resolves without sequelae over weeks, often recurring. Book: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) is the major form, lasts 4–6 weeks, mortality up to 30%; drugs are the commonest triggers (NSAIDs, sulfonamides, tetracycline, penicillin, doxycycline, anticonvulsants). Update: SJS/TEN are now separated from EM; mortality ~30% applies to toxic epidermal necrolysis (SJS is lower, under ~10%).

q: Which statement is TRUE?
o: The upper pole orifice tends to reflux
Horseshoe kidneys mostly fuse at upper poles
The lower pole ureter ends in a ureterocele
Horseshoe ascent is halted by the IMA
e: The fused lower poles cross ventral to the aorta and are trapped under the inferior mesenteric artery (IMA). Weigert-Meyer rule: the lateral, cephalad orifice drains the lower pole and may reflux; the medial, caudal orifice drains the upper pole and may have a ureterocele.

q: Which laparoscopic safety statement is FALSE?
o: Monopolar cautery is safest near bowel
Lower the pressure before removing trocars
Port leaks with high CO2 flow cool the child
Open or optical camera access is safer
e: Monopolar cautery raises the risk of unrecognised bowel injury. Lowering pressure before removing trocars reveals bleeding and stops omentum/bowel entering port sites. Large CO2 volumes from port leaks lower body temperature. Blind entry risks organ damage; bladeless optical trocars or open camera access help.

q: Which statement about the molecular response to renal obstruction is FALSE?
o: Fetal angiotensin acts mainly via AT1
MMP–TIMP balance sets ECM breakdown
EGF reduces apoptosis in obstruction
Renal renin rises in obstructed kidneys
e: Fetal angiotensin acts mainly through AT2 until late gestation, when AT1 grows in importance; it regulates growth, mediates fibrosis and modulates inflammation, and is altered by obstruction. Renal renin rises. EGF reduces apoptosis and growth impairment. ECM depends on synthesis and breakdown (MMPs vs TIMPs, regulated by TGF-β and angiotensin); fibrosis is universal. Epithelial–mesenchymal transformation is bidirectional and explains α-smooth muscle actin in obstruction (not part of normal glomerular development).

q: Which statement about periprostatic anatomy is FALSE?
o: Prostatic fascia fuses with levator fascia
Denonvilliers is thickest at the apex
The dorsal vein has three main branches
Three fascial layers cover the prostate
e: Denonvilliers fascia is densest at the base and over the seminal vesicles, thinning caudally to end at the striated sphincter. Dorsal vein: a superficial midline branch and two lateral branches. Three layers: Denonvilliers, prostatic and levator fasciae; laterally the prostatic fascia fuses with the levator fascia.

q: Which statement is FALSE?
o: Low-potency topical steroids suit genital psoriasis
PUVA is first choice for genital psoriasis
Systemic steroids speed lichen planus clearance
Reiter syndrome is linked to HLA-B27
e: Psoriasis affects up to 2%; genital disease is treated with short courses of low-potency topical steroids (book example: 3% liquor carbonis detergens in 1% hydrocortisone). High-dose PUVA raises genital SCC risk, so shield genitals; PUVA is contraindicated for genital lesions. Reiter syndrome (now reactive arthritis): urethritis, arthritis, conjunctivitis, oral ulcers, skin lesions after urethritis or GI infection; commoner with HIV; HLA-B27. Lichen planus: asymptomatic genital lesions need no treatment; topical steroids first; systemic steroids cut clearance from 29 to 18 weeks.

q: Which statement about UPJ obstruction is FALSE?
o: Kidneys under 15% function rarely recover
Intrinsic UPJO has longitudinal muscle bundles
UPJ obstruction may coexist with reflux
Most neonatal unilateral HN needs repair
e: Carefully followed neonatal unilateral hydronephrosis needs pyeloplasty in only about 7%. Intrinsic obstruction: an aperistaltic segment where spiral muscle is replaced by longitudinal bundles and fibrous tissue. UPJO may coexist with VUR. Repair indications: symptoms, impaired function, stones, infection, hypertension. In adults, kidneys with <15% function are generally not salvageable.

q: Which statement about SNM lead placement is TRUE?
o: S3 gives bellows and great toe flexion
Urodynamics reliably predict a response
S4 causes rotation of the whole leg
S3 lies about 13 cm above the coccyx
e: S3: levator 'bellows' contraction plus ipsilateral great toe flexion (plantar), with a pulling sensation in rectum, scrotum or vagina. (The book's keyed option says 'dorsiflexion'; the standard description is plantar flexion of the great toe.) S2: leg/hip rotation and anal clamp; S4: bellows only. S3 is located by the cross-hair technique and simple measurements; 11 cm (from the anal verge) or 13 cm from the coccyx are too far and land near S2/S1. No urodynamic or other preclinical factor predicts response: a percutaneous or staged lead trial is the best predictor.

q: Which statement about bladder development is FALSE?
o: The urachus becomes the median umbilical ligament
Smooth muscle first appears at the bladder neck
Detrusor appears between weeks 7 and 12
Lineage studies trace trigone mainly to bladder
e: Between weeks 7 and 12, connective tissue condenses and smooth muscle appears first at the dome, then toward the neck. By week 12 the urachus becomes a fibrous cord, the median umbilical ligament. Cell lineage studies show the trigone forms mostly from bladder (urogenital sinus) smooth muscle with only a minor ureteral contribution, unlike the classic theory.

q: Which statement about lichen sclerosus (LS) is FALSE?
o: Biopsy helps exclude malignant change
BXO is its late, scarring stage
It is linked to non-HPV penile cancer
It is a variant of lichen planus
e: LS shares little with lichen planus or nitidus beyond itch and genital predilection. It is a scarring disorder with pallor, loss of architecture and hyperkeratosis; the late stage, balanitis xerotica obliterans, can involve the urethra and cause stricture. It is associated with penile SCC (especially non-HPV variants) and may be premalignant; biopsy confirms and excludes cancer. Standard first-line therapy is an ultrapotent topical steroid (e.g., clobetasol).

q: Which statement about dorsal vein complex (DVC) handling is FALSE?
o: Its proximal edges are oversewn in a V shape
Partial division best stops DVC bleeding
The fascia is opened only superficially
Pubic fixation of the sphincter is kept
e: For troublesome DVC bleeding, divide the complex completely over the urethra and oversew the end; partial division plus traction opens veins and worsens bleeding. Incise the endopelvic fascia superficially, just enough to expose the junction of the anterior apex and the DVC; keep the pubourethral component to preserve anterior sphincter fixation. Divide the complex with minimal blood loss and without injuring the striated sphincter (incontinence). Oversew the proximal edges in a V, not pulled together in the midline, which would advance the NVBs anteriorly.

q: Years after pyeloplasty, a child's differential function falls from 40% to 32% with good drainage. Most likely cause:
o: Ongoing occult pyelonephritis
Faster growth of the other kidney
Recurrent UPJ obstruction
Renal artery stenosis after repair
e: The affected kidney cannot raise its absolute function as fast as the healthy kidney, so relative uptake falls: a relative, not absolute, loss. Still, 20–40% of post-obstructed kidneys deteriorate: reduced nephron number causes hyperfiltration, glomerulosclerosis and decline, and without functional reserve creatinine rises as the child grows.

q: Which endoureterotomy incision direction is correct?
o: Primary UPJ: anterior wall
Distal ureter: posterior
Mid ureter: medial side
Proximal ureter: lateral
e: Proximal ureteral strictures are incised laterally (or posterolaterally), like the UPJ; posterior incision is used for UPJO after failed open pyeloplasty. Mid and distal strictures are incised anteriorly (anteromedially, away from iliac vessels). Left ureteroenteric strictures do poorly endoscopically (more mobilisation, poorer blood supply); open repair succeeds in about 80%.

q: Which statement about genital duct development is FALSE?
o: Leydig cells secrete MIS
Testosterone drives wolffian ducts
Gartner cysts are wolffian remnants
Appendix testis is a müllerian remnant
e: Sertoli cells, differentiating in response to SRY, secrete MIS, which makes the paramesonephric (müllerian) ducts regress between weeks 8 and 10; these ducts form lateral to the mesonephric ducts. Leydig cell testosterone makes the wolffian ducts form the vas deferens and seminal vesicles. Müllerian remnants in males: prostatic utricle, appendix testis. Without MIS and androgens, müllerian ducts form tubes, uterus and upper two-thirds of the vagina; wolffian remnants are the epoophoron, paroophoron and Gartner duct cysts. The hymen forms at the junction of the vaginal plate and urogenital sinus.

q: Which statement about Behçet disease (BD) is FALSE?
o: Its genital ulcers are painless
Oral plus genital aphthae suggest BD
Uveitis is part of its classic triad
Neurologic disease takes priority over ulcers
e: Classic triad: oral and genital mucocutaneous lesions and uveitis; ulcers are painful. Relapsing, remitting, with genetic predisposition and autoimmune pathogenesis; may include epididymitis, thrombophlebitis, aneurysms, GI, neurologic and arthritic disease. Exclude aphthae, syphilis, herpes and chancroid first. Book case: seizures plus a painful genital ulcer: neurology review of his antiseizure treatment comes first.

q: In fetal obstructive uropathy, which finding suggests irreversible renal damage?
o: No calyceal dilatation
Very hypotonic fetal urine
Low urine calcium level
Urine sodium close to serum
e: Fetal urine sodium, chloride, osmolality and calcium correlate with fetal renal function; values approaching serum suggest irreversible damage (commonly quoted favourable values: Na <100 mmol/L, Cl <90 mmol/L, osmolality <200 mOsm/L). Distinct calyces help judge obstruction: no caliectasis suggests mild or minimal functional obstruction.

q: A woman with OAB failed drugs and then sacral neuromodulation. The most logical next step is:
o: Add a contralateral sacral lead
Intradetrusor botulinum toxin A
Switch to bilateral S3 leads now
Augmentation cystoplasty at once
e: She should already have failed anticholinergic or β3-agonist therapy. Botulinum toxin A is as good as SNM (ROSETTA trial, 2016: slightly greater reduction in urgency incontinence at 6 months, with more UTIs and self-catheterisation). Bilateral stimulation is logical (animal data) but the only clinical study (Scheepens 2002) showed no difference for urgency incontinence; retention patients voided better volumes with bilateral leads. No prospective trial supports a contralateral lead.

q: In open retropubic radical prostatectomy, the commonest site of a positive margin is:
o: The bladder neck
The posterior surface
The posterolateral side
The prostatic apex
e: The anterior apical surface is hard to identify during division of the striated sphincter–dorsal vein complex; seeing the exact anterior plane avoids entering the prostate and minimises sphincter excision. Order: apex, then posterior, then posterolateral.

q: Which statement about surgery for vesicoureteral reflux is FALSE?
o: A negative on-table cystogram proves cure
Needle entry point matters in injection
Tunnel length should be 5× ureter width
Endoscopic injection has its own learning curve
e: Under anaesthesia the child cannot void, so a negative intraoperative cystogram does not show success. Extravesical, intravesical and endoscopic (bulking agent) options all exist. Every technique creates a valve that compresses the ureter with filling and contraction: a submucosal tunnel with muscular backing, length about five times the ureteral diameter. Accurate needle entry and placement determine injection success; its learning curve differs from open surgery. Laparoscopic/robotic advantages: small incisions, less pain, short stay, quick recovery.

q: Which statement is FALSE?
o: Dapsone treats dermatitis herpetiformis
Asboe-Hansen sign occurs in pemphigus
Untreated pemphigus usually resolves alone
Extensive seborrhoeic dermatitis needs HIV test
e: Severe untreated pemphigus vulgaris can be fatal (loss of epidermal barrier); treat with systemic steroids plus steroid-sparing azathioprine or cyclophosphamide. Asboe-Hansen sign: fluid spreads under adjacent skin from pressure on a blister. Seborrhoeic dermatitis: demarcated pink-yellow scaly plaques; extensive disease suggests HIV. Dermatitis herpetiformis: coeliac/gluten, granular IgA at the basement membrane; dapsone and gluten-free diet. Linear IgA bullous dermatosis: circumferential and linear blisters; dapsone or sulfapyridine; 30–60% long-term remission.

q: Which statement about pyeloplasty is FALSE?
o: The anastomosis must be watertight, tension-free
Most laparoscopic failures appear by 2 years
Retroperitoneal access gives more working room
A funnel-shaped dependent UPJ is the aim
e: Transperitoneal laparoscopic pyeloplasty gives more working space and familiar anatomy, so it is the most used. Any repair needs a widely patent, watertight, tension-free anastomosis with a funnel-shaped, dependent UPJ. 70% of laparoscopic pyeloplasty failures occur within 2 years.

q: Which statement about prostate development is FALSE?
o: It buds from the urogenital sinus at 10–12 weeks
Its growth needs DHT made by 5α-reductase
It requires müllerian-inhibiting substance
Bulbourethral glands share its origin
e: Prostatic buds arise from the pelvic urethra (urogenital sinus) at 10–12 weeks, induced by mesenchyme under androgens; DHT from 5α-reductase is essential (deficiency severely impairs growth); MIS has no direct role. Prostate and bulbourethral glands come from the urogenital sinus; vas and appendix epididymis from the mesonephric duct; testis from the gonadal ridge. Androgen receptor defects cause abnormal masculinisation of external genitalia.

q: Which statement is FALSE?
o: PG is associated with inflammatory bowel disease
Factitial dermatitis is self-inflicted
Pyoderma gangrenosum has a diagnostic biopsy
Hailey-Hailey disease worsens with heat
e: Pyoderma gangrenosum (PG): painful ulcers with purulent base and tissue loss; linked to IBD, arthritis, collagen vascular and myeloproliferative disease; women in 2nd–5th decades; likely autoimmune. As in Behçet, no lab test or histology is pathognomonic. Hailey-Hailey: autosomal dominant intertriginous blistering (groin, perianal) with itch, pain and odour, worse in summer; inframammary disease common, vulvar unusual; excision and grafting, dermabrasion or laser for resistant disease. Factitial dermatitis: unconscious self-inflicted lesions, linked to borderline personality disorder.

q: Which statement about neurovascular bundle release is FALSE?
o: High anterior release lowers margin risk
Release starts on the posterior surface
The prostate is rolled, not pulled up
The posterior sphincter is muscle and fibrous tissue
e: High anterior release reduces traction on, and avoids cutting, anterior nerve branches to the cavernous bodies and sphincter, speeding recovery; but less apical soft tissue may raise the margin risk. Roll the prostate side to side with a sponge stick, with no upward traction. After developing the midline rectoprostatic plane, release the bundle from apex to base with a right angle starting on the posterior (rectal) surface, leaving Denonvilliers and prostatic fascia on the prostate. Dividing the posterior urethral band exposes the posterior sphincter complex (skeletal muscle and fibrous tissue).

q: Which statement about SNM problems is FALSE?
o: Switching off the IPG separates pocket pain
Lead heating is the main concern in MRI
Lost effect may reflect lead migration
Infected IPGs are saved by antibiotics
e: An infected implanted pulse generator (IPG) harbours biofilm, and infection can track along the lead to the sacrum: remove the whole device. MRI: main concern is lead heating damaging vessels or nerve roots; MRI and pregnancy are relative contraindications (book). Update: newer sacral systems are MRI-conditional for full-body scans. IPG pain: switch off; persistent pain means pocket causes (infection, waistline site, tight/loose pocket, seroma, erosion); pain that stops means output causes (unipolar sensitivity, current leak with abnormal impedance). Recurrent symptoms: check stimulation perception (wrong site, none or intermittent from migration, loose connection, high impedance).

q: Which statement about external genital development is FALSE?
o: Urethral folds form the labia majora
Both sexes look alike until 8 weeks
The genital tubercle forms from cloacal folds
Without DHT the folds do not fuse
e: Cloacal folds (5th week) meet anterior to the cloacal membrane as the genital tubercle; after cloacal division they become urogenital folds anteriorly and anal folds posteriorly; labioscrotal folds appear lateral to them. Without DHT the perineum does not lengthen and the folds do not fuse: labioscrotal folds become labia majora, urethral folds labia minora, the phallus the clitoris, and the urogenital sinus the vestibule.

q: Which statement is FALSE?
o: Early post-reimplant obstruction needs redo
Primary megaureter has an adynamic distal segment
Secondary reflux follows high bladder pressure
Recurrent VUR may reflect neuropathic bladder
e: Early obstruction after reimplant is common (oedema, subtrigonal bleeding, spasms, mucus, clots), usually mild and self-limiting; symptomatic cases present at 1–2 weeks with pain and vomiting. Observe; place a nephrostomy or stent for unabating symptoms. Distal ureteral devascularisation can cause fibrosis and recurrent obstruction. Besides technical error, recurrence often reflects unrecognised neuropathic bladder or severe voiding dysfunction. Obstructive megaureter: adynamic juxtavesical segment. Secondary reflux: neurogenic/non-neurogenic voiding dysfunction or outlet obstruction (e.g., valves).

q: Which pairing of UPJ technique and indication is FALSE?
o: Foley Y-V plasty: crossing lower pole vessel
Ureterocalicostomy: failed repair, small pelvis
Spiral flap: long narrow ureteric segment
Dismembered pyeloplasty: crossing vessel
e: Foley Y-V plasty suits a high ureteral insertion; it is contraindicated when lower pole vessels need transposition and of little use when the pelvis needs reduction. Flaps bridge longer narrow segments (spiral flap for the longest) and are unsuitable with crossing vessels. Only dismembered pyeloplasty transposes the UPJ relative to crossing vessels. Ureterocalicostomy (to the lower calyx) is salvage after failed pyeloplasty with a small pelvis.

q: Which statement is FALSE?
o: Trichomycosis is caused by Corynebacterium
Hot-tub folliculitis is usually pseudomonal
Fournier gangrene is mostly S. pyogenes
Erysipelas has a raised, sharp border
e: Fournier gangrene is polymicrobial (gram-positive, gram-negative, anaerobes). Erysipelas (usually Streptococcus pyogenes) involves dermis and lymphatics with a raised distinct border, unlike cellulitis. Folliculitis: perifollicular pustules in hairy areas, worsened by shaving; hot tubs/pools: Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Trichomycosis (axillary/pubic hair, hyperhidrosis): shaving, antibacterial soap, clindamycin gel, bacitracin, oral erythromycin. Hidradenitis suppurativa: follicular disorder of apocrine skin; follicular rupture (keratin, bacteria) drives inflammation, abscesses and sinuses; infection is not the initiator. Ecthyma gangrenosum: pseudomonal septicaemia with gangrenous ulcers.

q: Which statement about preserving the neurovascular bundle (NVB) is FALSE?
o: A posterior arterial branch is ligated first
Thermal energy near the bundles is avoided
The decision is fixed before surgery
A bundle fixed to the prostate is excised
e: The final decision is made at surgery, even after the prostate is out: inadequate tissue on the posterolateral specimen prompts secondary wide excision. Other indications: palpable induration in the lateral pelvic fascia, or a bundle fixed to the prostate. Book: never use thermal energy on or near the NVBs. Ligate the prominent posterior arterial branch running from the bundle over the seminal vesicles to the base; the bundles then fall back.

q: Which statement about diuretic renography is TRUE?
o: A T½ of 15 min excludes obstruction
DTPA is the preferred infant agent
T½ over 20 min suggests obstruction
MAG3 is cleared mainly by filtration
e: 99mTc-MAG3 is the usual agent: taken up and excreted rapidly by tubules, little filtration. Book: T½ >20 min presumed obstructed, <10 min normal, 10–20 min indeterminate. Other factors (hydration, bladder filling, diuretic timing, function, infant age) affect T½, which is less reliable in infants.

q: Which statement about sacral anterior root stimulation (Brindley) is FALSE?
o: It suits a long-term areflexic bladder
Posterior rhizotomy is usually added
It needs a bladder able to contract
It relies on post-stimulus voiding
e: Main use: inefficient or absent reflex micturition after spinal cord injury. Prerequisites: intact pathways from sacral pelvic-nerve nuclei to the bladder, and a bladder that can contract. Electrodes go intra- or extradurally on S2–S4 roots, activated independently. Usually complete posterior rhizotomy abolishes reflex incontinence, improves compliance and avoids co-contraction. Poststimulus voiding (Jonas and Tanagho): the striated sphincter relaxes faster than the detrusor between pulse trains. Current spread can cause pain, defecation, leg contraction, erection and ejaculation; pressure rise is not coordinated with bladder neck opening. Very effective but invasive and irreversible; future versions should avoid dorsal rhizotomy.

q: Which statement about gonadal development is FALSE?
o: SRY lies on the short arm of chromosome Y
Germ cells reach T10 level in the 5th week
SRY moved onto an X gives an XX male
SRY makes the wolffian ducts regress
e: SRY makes primitive sex cord cells become Sertoli cells, triggering testicular development; it does not regress the wolffian ducts (they regress without testosterone). In week 5 primordial germ cells migrate from the yolk sac along the dorsal mesentery to near T10, prompting genital ridge formation. SRY is on Yp; only about 25% of human sex reversals are due to SRY mutations (book). SRY translocated to an X gives an XX individual male characteristics.

q: Which statement about paediatric UPJ obstruction is FALSE?
o: Dysplasia is its commonest association
Crossing lower pole vessels may obstruct
Failed pyeloplasty may be redone open
Intrinsic muscle defects are one cause
e: Commonest associated anomaly: contralateral UPJO, then dysplasia and MCDK. Causes: intrinsic (interrupted circular muscle, altered collagen) or extrinsic (aberrant, accessory or early-branching lower pole vessel anterior to the UPJ). Complications: prolonged drainage, no functional or washout improvement, sometimes worse hydronephrosis/function; manage endoscopically or preferably by redo dismembered pyeloplasty.

q: Which statement is FALSE?
o: Lindane carries CNS toxicity in children
Tinea cruris typically affects scrotum
Permethrin 5% is first choice for scabies
Scrotal involvement suggests candidiasis
e: Tinea cruris (jock itch) affects the inner thighs and groin, usually sparing scrotum and penis; scrotal disease suggests Candida. Dermatophytes: Trichophyton, Microsporum, Epidermophyton; post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation may persist without active infection. Scabies (as for pediculosis pubis): 5% permethrin whole body overnight, repeated after 1 week. Lindane is disfavoured: CNS toxicity in children and rising resistance. (Oral ivermectin is a common alternative.)

q: Which statement is FALSE?
o: Small intrarenal pelvis bars ileal ureter
Psoas hitch may divide contralateral SVA
The genitofemoral nerve lies on the psoas
Boari flap needs normal bladder function
e: With a small intrarenal pelvis, ileocalycostomy can still be done. In a psoas hitch, dividing the contralateral superior vesical artery helps reach the ureter tension-free; avoid the genitofemoral nerve on the psoas. Normal bladder function without significant outlet obstruction is needed for ileal ureter, psoas hitch, Boari flap and reimplantation (not for endoscopic incision). If drain output rises after Foley removal, replace the catheter for some days (reflux up the stent, extravasation).

q: Which statement about the vesicourethral anastomosis in open RP is FALSE?
o: Tension is solved by firmer traction
Mucosa-to-mucosa apposition is the aim
A Babcock clamp has cut neck contractures
Free bladder from peritoneum if tense
e: Tie the anterior suture first; there should be no tension; if there is, release the bladder from the peritoneum. A Babcock clamp approximating bladder neck and urethra while sutures are tied virtually eliminated contractures (book series). Advance bladder mucosa so the anastomosis is mucosa to mucosa, watertight and tension-free.

q: Which statement is FALSE?
o: Tibial implants need no large battery
PTNS is the best-studied peripheral method
PTNS has a sham-controlled efficacy trial
IVES works by direct efferent stimulation
e: Intravesical electrical stimulation (IVES) acts by field stimulation of Aδ afferents from low-threshold bladder mechanoreceptors (Jiang 1998). Percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation (PTNS): sham-controlled trial (Peters 2010, SUmiT); evoked potentials suggest long-term central change (Finazzi Agrò 2009); relates to acupuncture point SP6; causes ipsilateral toe flexion; FDA approved; urodynamic predictors scarce. No direct comparisons of PTNS vs implanted tibial devices or vs SNM; tibial implants are small and battery-free. Electrical stimulation in LUT dysfunction is in its infancy; almost any LUT nerve could be used; new methods and sites keep emerging, with friendlier techniques coming.

q: Which statement about testicular descent is TRUE?
o: It enters the scrotum by month five
Abdominal pressure plays no part in transit
Spina bifida does not raise cryptorchidism
Testis is at the internal ring by month 3
e: The testis reaches the internal ring by the third month and traverses the canal to the scrotum between the 7th and 9th months. Abdominal pressure appears important for inguinal transit, which is why boys with spina bifida have a 23% incidence of cryptorchidism.

q: Which statement about premalignant penile lesions is FALSE?
o: Verrucous carcinoma links to HPV 6 and 11
Bowen disease is driven by HPV 6 and 11
PEKMB may coexist with verrucous cancer
Bowenoid papulosis is linked to HPV 16
e: Bowen disease on mucosal male genitalia is erythroplasia of Queyrat; HPV 8, 16, 39 and 51 co-infection has been found there. Verrucous carcinoma is linked to HPV 6/11, not 16/18. Bowenoid papulosis: multiple small red papules, HPV 16. Pseudoepitheliomatous keratotic micaceous balanitis (PEKMB): thick hyperkeratotic glans plaque in older men; premalignant status debated; concurrent verrucous carcinoma reported. Book: penile CIS rarely progresses. Caution: erythroplasia of Queyrat is usually quoted as progressing to invasive SCC in up to about 10–30%.

q: Which statement is FALSE?
o: Autotransplant can bridge long upper loss
Refluxing and non-refluxing reimplants match
Ileal ureter is avoided if creatinine >2
TUU suits a patient with recurrent stones
e: Transureteroureterostomy (TUU) is relatively contraindicated by stones, retroperitoneal fibrosis, urothelial cancer, chronic pyelonephritis and pelvic radiation. Book case (5 cm upper defect, small bladder, stones, creatinine >2 mg/dL): ureteroureterostomy, Boari flap, TUU and ileal ureter all unsuitable, so autotransplantation. In adults, refluxing and non-refluxing reimplants preserve function equally. About 25% renal function is needed to keep a UPJ or ureteral repair open.

q: Which statement about complications of open RP is FALSE?
o: Omentum is interposed after rectal repair
Pelvic haematoma can cause neck contracture
Re-exploration lowers incontinence risk
Hypotension needing blood is just observed
e: Patients needing acute transfusion for hypotension after RP should be re-explored to evacuate the pelvic haematoma, lowering the risk of bladder neck contracture and incontinence. After repairing a rectal injury, interpose omentum between the rectal closure and the anastomosis to prevent a rectourethral fistula.

q: Which statement is FALSE?
o: Classic KS favours the lower limbs
Sézary syndrome is leukaemic CTCL
Radiotherapy may transform verrucous cancer
EPD has another cancer in over 60%
e: Extramammary Paget disease (EPD): intraepithelial adenocarcinoma of apocrine sites; another underlying cancer in 10–30% (urethral, bladder, rectal, apocrine). Verrucous carcinoma: slow, exophytic, low-grade, rarely metastasises; uncircumcised glans/prepuce; local excision; primary radiotherapy relatively contraindicated (anaplastic transformation). Kaposi sarcoma: classic type on lower limbs, genitalia seldom; in AIDS a solitary genital lesion may be first; transplant-associated KS may resolve with altered immunosuppression; neoplastic vs hyperplastic debated. Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma: pruritus mimicking benign dermatoses, then plaques, ulcers, tumours; blood involvement = Sézary syndrome.

q: Which statement about continence and tissue sparing in open RP is TRUE?
o: Bladder neck sparing reduces stricture rate
Seminal vesicle sparing improves continence
Seminal vesicle sparing has caused abscesses
Leakage is mostly sphincter deficiency
e: Post-RP incontinence is usually intrinsic sphincter deficiency. Book: seminal vesicle sparing did not improve continence, potency or margins, with no reported pelvic abscess; bladder neck sparing did not improve continence, potency, margins or strictures. Complete seminal vesicle excision is recommended for cancer control. Note: some meta-analyses report better early continence with bladder neck preservation.

q: Which statement is FALSE?
o: Conduit hydronephrosis means obstruction
Ureteric strictures need cancer excluded
Repair places the ureter ventral to the IVC
Retrocaval ureter is a venous anomaly here
e: Most patients with long-term conduits have some non-obstructive hydronephrosis. Retrocaval ureter results from persistence of the posterior cardinal veins; repair transects the ureter and relocates it ventral to the IVC. Always rule out malignancy in a ureteral stricture.

q: Which statement about benign genital lesions is FALSE?
o: Zoon balanitis is common after circumcision
Pearly penile papules are angiofibromas
Eruptive seborrhoeic keratoses signal cancer
Fordyce angiokeratomas may bleed
e: Zoon (plasma cell) balanitis affects uncircumcised men from the 3rd decade; biopsy shows reactive epithelium with dermal plasma cells; exclude SCC and EPD; circumcision prevents and cures most cases (steroids or laser if refused). Pearly penile papules are angiofibromas like facial lesions of tuberous sclerosis. Angiokeratomas of Fordyce: 1–2 mm red-purple ectasias that may bleed. Skin tags (acrochordons) must be told from Birt-Hogg-Dubé fibrofolliculomas. Seborrhoeic keratoses spare mucosa, palms and soles; abrupt eruption (Leser-Trélat) marks internal malignancy. Epidermoid cysts are common in the scrotum.

q: Which statement about potency after open RP is FALSE?
o: Potency rose from 42% to 73% by 1 year
Sural grafts are laid in reversed position
An RCT showed sural grafts aid potency
Age and baseline potency affect recovery
e: A randomised study of sural nerve grafting when a bundle was sacrificed showed no difference; with bilateral grafts, 26% had full erections. Grafts are placed reversed (proximal to distal). Recovery depends on age, preoperative potency and bundle preservation; in one study 42% potent at 3 months, 73% at 1 year. Book: if PDE5 inhibitors are used, on-demand dosing is preferred to daily (trials such as REINVENT found no advantage for nightly dosing).

q: Which statement about retroperitoneal fibrosis (RPF) is FALSE?
o: Biopsy rarely helps exclude malignancy
Steroids are the usual first treatment
Many cases are immune-mediated aortitis
Raised ESR predicts a steroid response
e: Malignant RPF is often indistinguishable from idiopathic RPF; only biopsy showing tumour islands identifies it. Most cases are immune-mediated aortitis (many now recognised as IgG4-related disease). CT: soft tissue around the aorta and IVC effacing the planes between them (perianeurysmal fibrosis if aneurysm). Steroids first, more likely to help with active inflammation (high ESR, leukocytosis, lymphocytes on biopsy); also azathioprine, cyclophosphamide, ciclosporin, colchicine, tamoxifen (rituximab is used in IgG4 disease).

q: Which statement about complications of open RP is FALSE?
o: Bladder neck contracture is under 10%
Inguinal hernia follows in under 2%
Hernias after RP are usually indirect
Rectal injury rates have fallen sharply
e: 15–20% develop an inguinal hernia, usually indirect. Bladder neck contractures occur in <10%. Of complication rates, only rectal injury has changed dramatically.

q: Which statement is FALSE?
o: Wait 3 months after TURP for surgery
Salvage RP needs truly localised disease
Salvage RP keeps potency in most men
Wait 6–8 weeks after biopsy for surgery
e: Defer RP 6–8 weeks after biopsy and 3 months after TURP. Salvage RP only for unequivocally localised cancer; complications: incontinence 50%, anastomotic stricture 24%, near-universal erectile dysfunction, about 45% recurrence at 5 years.

q: Which step in open RP and pelvic lymphadenectomy is correct?
o: Keep the hypogastric veins unexposed
Clip pudendal perforators at the fascia
Ligate the obturator vein routinely
Clear lymphatics over the external iliac
e: Obturator artery and vein are skeletonised but left unless bleeding; dissection goes down to the pelvic floor, exposing the hypogastric veins. Preserve the lymphatics on the external iliac artery (they drain the leg). On extending the endopelvic incision toward the puboprostatic ligaments, clip small pudendal branches perforating the pelvic muscle to avoid coagulation injury to the pudendal artery and nerve beneath.

q: Which statement about radical perineal prostatectomy is FALSE?
o: Rectal injury occurs in about 1% to 5%
Leg neurapraxia is usually transient only
Rectal manipulation is avoided after it
Lowsley traction helps rectourethralis cut
e: Upward traction on the Lowsley tractor while dividing the rectourethralis tents the rectum and causes injury; an assistant should press gently downward, and traction waits until after division. Rectal injury: 1–5% in most series (one 11%); repaired at once the operation proceeds; unrecognised it can form a fistula. Lower limb sensory neurapraxia ~2% (one series 25%), more than retropubic, almost always transient; motor deficit rare. Rapid diet, early walking, most home by day 2; no rectal manipulation. A red rubber catheter guides the anterior sutures; the Foley goes in only after they are tied; interrupted sutures; tennis-racquet neck reconstruction if needed.
